findings.title: Measured document grip
findings.claim: Within the declared pericope, the focus creation statement can also be read as measured formation of a joined, strengthened text made governable by the hand.
findings.mechanism: The focus verb خَلَقْتُكَ carries the supplied measured-boundary branch. It meets the 19:12 command to take the Book with strength, where taking supplies hand contact, the Book supplies a joined written object, and gathered strength supplies the rope-strand image; the count three at 19:10 adds a bounded three-part structural cue.
findings.reader_payoff: The later command to take the Book gives the earlier creation answer a material contour: formation is not only emergence, but measured joining and secure handling.
findings.containment: The ordinary creation reading remains intact. The imperative خُذِ is not recast as a handle noun, the numeral ثَلَاثَ is not claimed to say that the Book literally has three parts, and no particular historical document or fabrication process is asserted.

epistemic.reason: The context roots, focus branch, branch images, and channel supports are supplied and citable, but the joining of them into one document scene is a multi-step pericope interpretation rather than a direct gloss of 19:9.

findings.title: First state transition
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the focus sequence from non-thing to created thing is the first instance of a pericope pattern that passes through birth, death, raising, and life.
findings.mechanism: The focus خَلَقْتُكَ at 19:9:9:1 supplies creative origination, while تَكُ at 19:9:13:1 and شَيْئًا at 19:9:14:1 mark the prior state and the threshold of thinghood. The 19:15 occurrences for birth, death, raising, and living supply independent later transitions that return to those focus state markers.
findings.reader_payoff: The phrase about once being nothing becomes a compact origin point in a larger sequence of state changes rather than only a one-time analogy for the unusual birth.
findings.containment: The focus still says that the addressee was created before and was not a thing. The transition pattern is a contextual model, not an assertion that 19:9 explicitly names resurrection, death, or the later life sequence.

epistemic.reason: The focus and 19:15 coordinates exactly match the supplied trace, but the cross-ayah state-transition model is explicitly exploratory and several branches have unresolved identities.
